title: Comparing & Job Perks
description: From your course: how much bigger, better or worse something is, what is useful or a waste of time, and the perks a job offers.

items.definition: informal: a much bigger amount, or much more, than something else
items.example: In my new job I've got [loads more] free time than I used to have.
items.exampleRu: На новой работе у меня гораздо больше свободного времени, чем раньше.
items.pattern: lots/loads more + noun (+ than); lots/loads + comparative (+ than)
items.trap: Informal: great with friends, not in a report or an email to a client. Say 'loads more', not 'loads of more'.

items.definition: used before a comparative to say that the difference is big
items.example: Going by train is [far more] relaxing than driving, and you can read on the way.
items.exampleRu: Ехать на поезде гораздо спокойнее, чем за рулём, и можно читать в дороге.
items.pattern: much/a lot/far + comparative (+ than)
items.trap: Before a comparative say 'much better' or 'far better', never 'very better' or 'more better'.

items.translation: даже близко не такой …, как … / далеко не так …, как … (нейтр.)
items.definition: not nearly as …; a lot less … than
items.example: The sequel was [nowhere near as] good as the first film.
items.exampleRu: Продолжение было даже близко не таким хорошим, как первый фильм.
items.pattern: nowhere near as + adjective/adverb + as
items.trap: 'Nowhere near', not 'not near' or 'nowhere close as': 'It's nowhere near as hard as I thought.'

items.definition: not at all as …; far less … than
items.example: My new laptop is [nothing like as] noisy as the old one.
items.exampleRu: Мой новый ноутбук совсем не такой шумный, как старый.
items.pattern: nothing like as + adjective + as
items.trap: Keep both 'as': 'nothing like as cold as Moscow'. Leaving out the first 'as' is a common mistake.

items.definition: formal: used before a comparative to say that the difference is big; 'infinitely' means very much indeed
items.example: The new system is [significantly more] efficient than the old one, so reports take half the time.
items.exampleRu: Новая система существенно эффективнее старой, поэтому отчёты занимают вдвое меньше времени.
items.pattern: considerably/significantly/infinitely + comparative (+ than)
items.trap: Formal: good for reports, presentations and work emails. 'Infinitely better' is a strong, often emotional exaggeration.

items.term: a little / slightly / a bit (more) … than
items.ipa: ə ˈlɪtl / ˈslaɪtli / ə bɪt (mɔː) … ðən
items.definition: used before a comparative to say that the difference is small
items.example: The blue jacket is [slightly more] expensive than the black one, but it fits better.
items.exampleRu: Синяя куртка немного дороже чёрной, но сидит лучше.
items.pattern: a little/slightly/a bit + comparative (+ than)
items.trap: With short adjectives there is no 'more': 'a bit cheaper', not 'a bit more cheaper'. 'A bit' is the most informal of the three.

items.definition: nearly the same; only a little less … than
items.example: My daughter is already [almost as] tall as me.
items.exampleRu: Моя дочь уже почти такого же роста, как я.
items.pattern: almost/nearly as + adjective + as
items.trap: It's 'as … as', never 'as … than' or 'so … like': 'almost as good as the original'.

items.definition: formal: by a very small amount
items.example: This year's sales were only [marginally] higher than last year's.
items.exampleRu: Продажи в этом году лишь незначительно выше прошлогодних.
items.pattern: marginally + comparative (+ than)
items.trap: Formal: in conversation people say 'slightly' or 'a tiny bit'. It's an adverb, so 'marginally higher', not 'marginal higher'.

items.definition: exactly as …; to the same degree
items.example: Working from home can be [just as] tiring as going to the office.
items.exampleRu: Работа из дома может утомлять точно так же, как поездки в офис.
items.pattern: just as + adjective/adverb (+ as)
items.trap: With an adjective use 'as … as', not 'the same … as': 'just as tiring as', not 'the same tiring as'.

items.translation: ничуть не менее … (чем) / ровно такой же … (как)
items.definition: in every way as …; used to stress that something is not less good, important, etc.
items.example: The little café round the corner is [every bit as] good as the famous one, and half the price.
items.exampleRu: Маленькое кафе за углом ничуть не хуже знаменитого, а стоит вдвое меньше.
items.pattern: every bit as + adjective (+ as)
items.trap: A fixed phrase: 'every bit as', not 'each bit as' or 'every piece as'.

items.definition: to the same degree as each other
items.example: Both candidates were [equally] strong, so the decision took ages.
items.exampleRu: Оба кандидата были одинаково сильными, поэтому решение заняло кучу времени.
items.pattern: equally + adjective; (spoken) equally as + adjective (+ as)
items.trap: Safest: 'equally important' or 'just as important as'. 'Equally as … as' is common in speech, but teachers and editors often mark it wrong.

items.definition: to be very useful or important to someone
items.example: Your feedback has been really [valuable to] me as a new manager.
items.exampleRu: Твои отзывы были для меня, как для нового менеджера, очень ценными.
items.pattern: be valuable to sb / valuable for sth
items.trap: 'Valuable' means very useful or worth a lot. Careful with 'invaluable': it means even more useful, the opposite of what it looks like.

items.definition: to be extremely useful to someone
items.example: Her advice was [invaluable to] me when I started my own business.
items.exampleRu: Её советы были для меня бесценны, когда я открывал своё дело.
items.pattern: be invaluable to sb / invaluable for sb
items.trap: 'Invaluable' = extremely useful, NOT 'not valuable'. The opposite of 'valuable' is 'worthless'. And there is no word 'unvaluable'.

items.definition: to work well and give the result someone wants
items.example: That diet just wasn't [effective for] me, so I stopped after a month.
items.exampleRu: Мне эта диета просто не помогла, так что через месяц я её бросил.
collocations: an effective way to do sth
items.pattern: be effective for sb
items.trap: 'Effective' = it works and gives the result. 'Efficient' = it doesn't waste time or money. A slow but working method is effective, not efficient.

items.definition: to be successful at producing a result
items.example: Short daily lessons are [effective in] building a habit.
items.exampleRu: Короткие ежедневные занятия эффективно помогают выработать привычку.
items.pattern: be effective in doing sth / effective at doing sth
items.trap: After 'in' use the -ing form: 'effective in building', not 'effective in to build'. 'Effective at doing sth' is also fine.

items.definition: to help someone or be good for what they need
items.example: These phrases will be really [useful for] anyone moving to the UK.
items.exampleRu: Эти фразы будут очень полезны всем, кто переезжает в Великобританию.
items.pattern: be useful for sb / useful to sb
items.trap: 'Useful to sb' is fine too. For a thing you use, say 'useful for sth': 'useful for travel'.

items.definition: to help with doing something
items.example: Podcasts are [useful in] improving your listening skills.
items.exampleRu: Подкасты полезны для развития навыков восприятия на слух.
items.pattern: be useful in doing sth / useful for doing sth
items.trap: After a preposition use -ing: 'useful in improving', not 'useful in improve'. 'Useful for improving' also works.

items.definition: to be of no help to someone
items.example: Most of these apps are [useless for] complete beginners.
items.exampleRu: Большинство этих приложений бесполезны для полных новичков.
items.pattern: be useless for sb / useless to sb
items.trap: 'Useless to me' is fine too. But for a skill a person lacks, use 'at': 'I'm useless at cooking'.

items.definition: informal: to be very bad at doing something
items.example: I'm completely [useless at] remembering names.
items.exampleRu: Я совершенно не умею запоминать имена.
items.pattern: be useless at sth / at doing sth
items.trap: For skills use 'at', like 'good at' and 'bad at': 'I'm useless at cooking'. Russian 'в' makes people say 'in' here.

items.ipa: bi ə weɪst əv taɪm / ˈenədʒi
items.translation: быть пустой тратой времени / сил (для кого-то)
items.definition: to be not worth the time or effort it takes
items.example: Honestly, the whole meeting was [a waste of time] for most of us.
items.exampleRu: Честно говоря, вся эта встреча была для большинства из нас пустой тратой времени.
collocations: it's a waste of time doing sth
items.pattern: be a waste of time/energy/money (for sb)
items.trap: 'A waste of time', not 'a loss of time' (a calque of 'потеря времени').

items.definition: to not work or give the result someone wants
items.example: Painkillers are often [ineffective for] people with this kind of headache.
items.exampleRu: Обезболивающие часто не помогают людям с такой головной болью.
items.pattern: be ineffective for sb
items.trap: The opposite of 'effective' is 'ineffective', never 'uneffective'.

items.definition: to fail to produce the result that was wanted
items.example: The new parking rules have been [ineffective in] reducing traffic.
items.exampleRu: Новые правила парковки не помогли уменьшить пробки.
items.pattern: be ineffective in doing sth / ineffective at doing sth
items.trap: 'Ineffective', never 'uneffective'; and after 'in' comes the -ing form.

items.definition: to not help someone, or make things harder for them
items.example: Vague feedback is [unhelpful for] new employees.
items.exampleRu: Расплывчатые отзывы не помогают новым сотрудникам.
items.pattern: be unhelpful for sb / unhelpful to sb
items.trap: The opposite of 'useful' is 'useless'; of 'helpful' it's 'unhelpful'. There is no word 'unuseful'.

items.definition: things that make people want to work harder: money (a bonus, a pay rise) or other benefits (flexible hours, training)
items.example: Besides a good salary, [non-financial incentives] like flexible hours really matter to me.
items.exampleRu: Кроме хорошей зарплаты, для меня очень важны нефинансовые стимулы, например гибкий график.
collocations: a strong incentive to do sth
items.pattern: an incentive to do sth / an incentive for sb
items.trap: 'Incentives', not 'stimuli': 'stimulus' is about science or the economy, not about rewards at work.

items.definition: chances to move to a higher position at work
items.example: The pay is average, but the [promotional opportunities] are excellent.
items.exampleRu: Зарплата средняя, но возможности для карьерного роста отличные.
items.pattern: promotional opportunities / opportunities for promotion
items.trap: 'Opportunities', not 'possibilities'. In job ads you'll also see 'promotion opportunities' or 'opportunities for promotion'; 'promotional' alone can also mean advertising.

items.definition: a plan where you and your employer pay money regularly so that you get an income when you retire
items.example: The company pays into a [pension scheme] for every employee.
items.exampleRu: Компания делает взносы в пенсионную программу за каждого сотрудника.
items.pattern: pay into / join / opt out of a pension scheme
items.trap: British English says 'pension scheme'; Americans say 'pension plan'. Not 'pension programme'.

items.definition: extra money an employer pays once a year, usually for good results
items.example: If we hit our targets, everyone gets an [annual bonus] in December.
items.exampleRu: Если мы выполним план, в декабре все получат ежегодную премию.
items.pattern: get / receive / pay an annual bonus
items.trap: Extra money from your employer is a 'bonus'. A 'premium' is what you pay for insurance.

items.translation: бесплатный уход за детьми (детский сад от компании)
items.definition: looking after employees' young children at no cost, often in a nursery at work
items.example: Parents at my company get [free childcare] in a nursery next to the office.
items.exampleRu: Родители в нашей компании могут бесплатно оставлять детей в детском саду рядом с офисом.
items.pattern: free / affordable / on-site childcare
items.trap: 'Childcare' is one word and uncountable: 'free childcare', not 'a free childcare' or 'children care'.

items.definition: paying a gym so that you can use it, usually every month or year
items.example: My [gym membership] costs forty pounds a month, and I hardly ever go.
items.exampleRu: Мой абонемент в спортзал стоит сорок фунтов в месяц, а я почти не хожу.
items.pattern: have / get / cancel a gym membership
items.trap: Not 'abonement' or 'gym subscription': for a gym or a club it's 'membership'.
